note: Recast from Sands 1965 (a revision of the Ethiopian Nasutitermitinae), the original in English; the species is treated in that revision as the entry on page 114, with synonyms including Eutermes rhodesiensis Sjöstedt, 1911 (type locality Salisbury, Southern Rhodesia), E. brutus, E. agricola, E. rufonasalis, E. voseni, E. kalaharicus, Trinervitermes gemellus form kalaharicus, T. abassas, T. thermarum, E. diplacodes, E. muneris, E. loubetsiensis and others (mostly syn. n.). The soldier section takes only the shared generic description; the species-level soldier measurements are not transcribed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate: head capsule, middle of the frons and vertex brown to dark chestnut brown, the vertex with a yellow to brown pale median patch, sometimes indistinctly striped within; the region around the compound eyes and antennal sockets, in front of the ocelli and along the posterior margin of the postclypeus yellow to yellowish brown; postclypeus and labrum yellow to yellowish brown, antennae yellow. The posterior margin of the head capsule behind the compound eyes much less than a semicircle, slightly undulate immediately behind the compound eyes; fontanelle distinct, usually a slender Y, the lateral arms often (but not always) swollen at the tips; compound eyes short-oval, W/E index 2.8—3.4; ocelli 1/7 to 2/5 of their own minimum diameter from the compound eyes; postclypeus moderately arched, 2.2—2.5 times as wide as long; right mandibular molar plate with 7—8 ridges; antenna 15—16-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule, middle of the frons and vertex brown to dark chestnut brown; the vertex with a yellow to brown pale median patch, sometimes partly divided into indistinct stripes; the region around the compound eyes and antennal sockets, in front of the ocelli and along the posterior margin of the postclypeus yellow to yellowish brown; postclypeus and labrum yellow to yellowish brown, antennae yellow. Pronotum yellow to yellowish brown, the margins sometimes darker; mesonotum, metanotum, the other thoracic sclerites and the legs yellow. Abdominal tergites yellow to yellowish brown, brownish clouded around the spiracles, the median tergites sometimes with a narrow brown band between the spiracles; sternites yellow, yellowish brown around the spiracles. Wings translucent pale brown, the outlines of the subcosta and of the base of the radial sector brown, the outline of the posterior margin of the radial sector gradually becoming orange towards the apex; the wing membrane behind the radial sector with an orange stripe. The posterior margin of the head capsule behind the compound eyes much less than a semicircle, slightly undulate immediately behind the compound eyes; fontanelle distinct, usually a slender Y, the lateral arms often (but not always) swollen at the tips, its length often more than twice the basal width of the lateral arms; compound eyes short-oval, prominent relative to their own diameter and medium-sized relative to the head width, W/E index 2.8—3.4; ocelli medium-sized, 1/7 to 2/5 of their own minimum diameter from the compound eyes; postclypeus moderately arched, 2.2—2.5 times as wide as long, the anterior margin slightly concave, the posterior margin convex, the sides rather rounded, the median curvature flatter; right mandibular molar plate with 7—8 ridges; antenna 15—16-segmented, the variation of the basal segments in the two segment counts described separately in the original (in the 15-segmented form segments 2 and 5 subequal, segments 5 and 6 subequal and slightly longer, segment 3 longer than both; in the 16-segmented form segments 2 and 4 subequal, segments 3 and 6 subequal and slightly longer, segment 5 longer still). In the female the anterior margin of sternite 5 bears a pale 'odour' gland, in medium-sized individuals 0.69—0.90 mm wide and 0.13—0.23 mm long; the female cerci longer than broad at the base, conical. The pilosity of the vertex varies in length and does not form a 'felt' or a 'pad'. Measurements (mm, 30 heads, 10 localities): head width (including compound eyes) 1.60—1.84 (mean 1.70); maximum diameter of the compound eye 0.50—0.59 (mean 0.54); ocellus 0.16—0.23×0.21—0.30 (mean 0.19×0.25).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The original records in the generic description that the soldiers of this genus are mostly dimorphic, with a 'major' and a 'minor' form or a nearly continuous transition; nasus cylindrical to strongly conical; reduced mandibles usually without apical points; head capsule without a constriction behind the antennae and without conspicuous setae except on the nasus (major soldier), the head capsule of the minor soldier often with a constriction. The species-level description and measurements of the soldier of this species fall outside the OCR coverage of this work and are not recorded.
